case_title: Rakesh and Another v. State of Haryana
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (husband); Relative (mother-in-law). Prior dowry-related harassment and demands for money described.
statutory_provisions: IPC s.498A; IPC s.302 r/w s.34
evidence_type: Dying declaration; medical evidence (duty doctor, casualty medical officer, post-mortem); magistrate's testimony; father of victim's testimony; recovery of kerosene stove on disclosure
aggravating_circumstances: Victim beaten mercilessly, including a blow with a leg on the neck before being set on fire; prolonged dowry harassment; accused did not inform victim's parents or seek her transfer to a better hospital
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.498A IPC (RI one year, fine Rs.500 each) and s.302 r/w s.34 IPC (RI for life, fine Rs.2000 each); sentences concurrent
high_court_outcome: Appeal dismissed; conviction and sentence confirmed
offence_finally_established: IPC s.498A and IPC s.302 r/w s.34
neutral_facts: The victim had been married to one accused for about eight years and had four children. The victim's family had given dowry at the wedding, but the victim was allegedly harassed for more, including after a sister's wedding about fifteen days before the incident. On the night of 14 May 1998, around 11 p.m., a quarrel took place at the accused's house. It is alleged that one accused placed a leg on the victim's neck and beat the victim, after which the other accused held the victim's hands while the husband sprinkled kerosene and set the victim on fire with a match. A relative was present in the house. The victim was taken to hospital in the early hours of 15 May 1998. On 16 May 1998 a judicial magistrate, after a duty doctor certified the victim fit and conscious, recorded the victim's statement in question-and-answer form, with a toe impression, naming the husband and mother-in-law and describing the dowry harassment. The examining doctor recorded burns over approximately 85% of the body. The victim died of burn injuries on 4 June 1998 at another hospital, and the post-mortem attributed death to burns. Police arrested the husband on 21 May 1998, when he showed doctors burn injuries to his hands; a stove containing kerosene was recovered on his disclosure. The victim's father testified about the in-laws' harassment. A defence witness, a child of the accused, said the fire came from a kerosene stove but admitted the husband was present in the house at the time.
physical_harm: Superficial to deep burns over almost all the body except the legs below the knees (approx. 85%); death from burn injuries
motive: Accepted by the Court: dowry-related harassment and demands for money from the victim's father, including after a sister's wedding
key_evidence_accepted: Dying declaration recorded by the Judicial Magistrate after the duty doctor certified fitness; doctor's evidence on fitness and burns; Magistrate's evidence; post-mortem evidence of death from burns
witness_credibility: Magistrate (PW-10) and doctor (PW-6) assessed as reliable; alleged wrong names and presence of relatives held not material, as the Magistrate had directed relatives to leave
post_offence_conduct: Accused husband did not get treatment for his alleged hand burns on the day of the incident, only showing them to a doctor on arrest on 21.05.1998; accused did not inform victim's parents
trial_duration: offence: 14.05.1998; trial judgment: 27.09.2001 (conviction) and 28.09.2001 (sentence); High Court: 15.05.2006; Supreme Court: 22.03.2013
legal_representation: Accused: R.N. Kush, S.K. Sabharwal. State: Kamal Mohan Gupta, Mohd. Zahid Hussain
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; charges framed; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: None noted by the Court; presence of some relatives in the ward during recording was considered and held not to affect the declaration
appeal_history: Trial court: convicted and sentenced. High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction and sentence confirmed. Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
prosecution_argument: Dying declaration was validly recorded after fitness certification; husband's hand burns were no answer since he did not seek treatment on the day; the husband's burns showed doubt about his version
defence_argument: Victim was not fit to make a statement (85% burns), so the dying declaration could not support conviction; husband's burn injuries showed he came to rescue the victim, so it was improbable he set her on fire; alternatively, conviction should be altered to s.304 Part I
legal_principle_applied: Dying declaration acceptable where recording procedure, fitness, and corroborating doctor and Magistrate evidence are satisfied; minor discrepancies in names and presence of relatives are not material; proof beyond reasonable doubt
sentencing_rationale: Not stated as a separate sentencing rationale; Court declined to alter s.302 conviction to s.304 Part I given the death caused by burns at the accused's instance
judicial_aggravating_factors: Death occurred at the matrimonial home from burn injuries caused at the accused's instance; victim left four children
other_sentence_order: None. Note: second appellant released after 14 years on orders of the appropriate Government
